O.outcome_detail: experimentation with embedding shapes in woven designs

cells.quote: Findings show that as youth progressed from their first to their last project, 76% of participants shifted their practice to experiment with embedding shapes into their designs.
cells.note: The quoted 76% finding is not present in the supplied study-text excerpt; quote taken from the wiki entry. The study reports 13 participants, most with little or no prior weaving experience and two with prior experience.

cells.quote: All studies received favorable feedback and an improvement in technical metrics, such as decreased procedural and fluoroscopy time (LoE = 1-2/5).
cells.note: This is a systematic review synthesis of studies involving surgical trainees, vascular surgeons, and medical students; the comparison is pre-simulation performance where reported.

O.outcome_detail: procedure, fluoroscopy, and contrast use in real patients

cells.quote: The 3D printed Aneurysm model simulated patient-specific EVAR and differentiated operative performance between simulation trained and nontrained residents (relations to other variables rating = 2/2). Participants decreased procedure time, fluoroscopy time, and contrast used on real patients post simulator use (LoE = 3/5).
cells.note: The review reports transfer from simulation to real-patient EVAR performance.

O.outcome_detail: in-hospital mortality and major or minor errors

cells.quote: The same group achieved an LoE of 4/5 after EVAR rehearsal, as there was a reduction in major and minor errors post simulator use, having a direct effect on patient outcomes by reducing in-hospital mortality by 2%.
cells.note: The outcome is a clinical patient outcome rather than a learning-performance measure.

O.outcome_detail: retention of proficiency up to 3 months

cells.quote: Maertens et al. was awarded an LoE of 5/5 as proficiency levels were retained up to 3 mo, alongside an improvement in patient outcomes and better operative performance.
cells.note: The review reports retention after simulation training; the source text does not specify a separate randomized comparison group.
